+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -132,8 +132,14 @@
 the defaults and is scheduled for recording as such. `sources.consent` says which.
 
 The ledger producer sends JSON object envelopes with additive `version:1`, retaining complete records in independently readable chunks compatible with the existing consumer. Each body is at most120000 UTF-8 bytes; a batch contains at most100 messages and240000 body bytes, reserving platform headroom. An oversized individual record or serialization failure refuses the whole invocation before queue submission; nothing is trimmed. The internal helper receipt counts records and finalized messages as queue-acknowledged, acceptance-unknown, or not attempted. Failed preflight has `prepared:false`, zero planned messages and all records not attempted. A rejected queue group stops delivery: earlier acknowledgements remain, that group's acceptance is unknown, and the tail is not attempted. Missing queue capability is not attempted. One fixed-code/count-only failure diagnostic is emitted even when callers ignore the receipt; Analytics points are independent. Queue acceptance is not R2 persistence, client delivery, retry, recovery or completeness assurance. Durable recovery, deduplication and deployed performance remain separate work.
 
+With exact `LEDGER_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, producers opt into managed capture recovery; every other value retains the default legacy lane. Deploy recognizing consumers and the eraser before enabling producers; those readers recognize managed data regardless of the flag. Frozen envelopes receive opaque delivery UUIDs independent of logical event IDs. Queue failure, missing capability or an oversized queue row can fall back to the same canonical R2 sink, without re-enqueueing. The separate `capture` receipt conserves `newlyStored`, `alreadyPresent`, `suppressed`, `unknown` and `notAttempted` records. A failed/ambiguous write is not rollback. Unserializable records cannot be recovered, and bodies above the16MiB canonical limit are refused, never trimmed. The single sanitized diagnostic includes capture disposition.
+
+Managed NDJSON preserves every original field and adds reserved `_ledger_delivery: {id, ordinal}` provenance. Reusing one delivery UUID with conflicting content/partition refuses; distinct delivery UUIDs are not collapsed merely because logical IDs match. Metadata-only identity commitments and immutable destination claims live under `ledger-delivery/identities/` and `ledger-delivery/claims/`, outside canonical tenant/date scans; they are not a raw-data outbox or an approved retention lifecycle. New deliveries retain grouped tenant/hour/stream objects, bounded by100 delivery parts and16MiB. Conditional append retries at most three precondition conflicts, re-reading the object and current rewrite/tombstone barriers each time; thrown storage errors are terminal. Managed erasure preserves metadata and uses conditional replacement, including an empty body instead of deleting an emptied managed object. A conflicting body or precondition failure leaves its durable intent pending for recovery, without automatic rebase or guessed removal credit; exact after-state reconciliation handles a lost acknowledgement.
+
+This is bounded local capture recovery, not completeness: process death before acknowledged capture, legacy/old-consumer retries, DLQ/quarantine, SDK logical-event collisions, late-hour fold repair, exceptional object fragmentation and deployed performance remain open. Fresh barrier checks are not an atomic global erasure fence; pre-cutoff races, ETag ABA, concurrent journal coordination and manifest omissions remain limitations. Claim lifecycle/retention and operational activation require their respective approvals; the flag is default-off and no deployment is implied.
+
 ## 3. Identity
 
 All under `/v1/{tenant}/identity/`. The first two take the site key; the rest take the operator token.
